title.title: Circulant Hadamard matrices exist only in orders 1 and 4
title.subtitle: Claim: Ryser's 1963 conjecture holds, so Barker sequences exist exactly at lengths 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 13

plain: Can a row of pluses and minuses, shifted around, stay perfectly out of step with itself? Only in tiny cases

panels.caption: order 4: each row is the one above, shifted cyclically

beats.text: Four cyclic shifts of one $\pm 1$ row, pairwise orthogonal: a circulant Hadamard matrix
Barker sequences: every off-peak autocorrelation is $0$ or $\pm 1$
The claim settles both: no circulant order beyond 4, no Barker length beyond 13

steps: Classical arithmetic forces the order to be $4u^2$, $u$ odd
Character values then multiply to a root of unity
A 2-adic computation shows that fails unless $u = 1$

achievement.label: Ryser's circulant Hadamard conjecture (1963)
achievement.context: Before: any other order is $4u^2$ with $u$ odd; 4,489 candidates were left below $4 \cdot 10^{30}$
achievement.note: Odd Barker lengths rest on Turyn–Storer, cited, not formalized

verify.detail: The circulant statement and the even-length Barker statement are both formal
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean statement; we did not build it

voice.text: Every shift of this plus-minus row is orthogonal. Ryser bet only order four works.
Arithmetic forces a special order, then a two-adic check rules it out.
Claimed: only orders one and four.

A real circulant Hadamard matrix of order n >= 1 exists iff n in {1,4}
